item.title: A Plan for Two Dans: How Democrats Manipulated Alaska’s Ballot
item.description: An investigation by The New York Times looked at how two people named Dan Sullivan ended up on the ballot for the Senate.
item.dc:creator: Michael Barbaro, Kellen Browning, Lexie Diao, Anna Foley, Carlos Prieto, Eric Krupke, Maria Byrne, Paige Cowett, Elisheba Ittoop, Dan Powell, Marion Lozano and Chris Wood
item.media:description: A sample Alaska election ballot.

item.title: Four Scenarios for How the Midterms Could Go
item.description: Expectations are cresting for Democrats, and some kind of wave seems likely, but so much will depend on a few close Senate races.
item.dc:creator: Nate Cohn

item.title: A Clash Over Trans Women in Sports Erupts at a Pro Soccer Game
item.description: For protesters seeking a ban on transgender athletes in women’s sports, it made sense to protest near fans of the Portland Thorns, who are known for progressive politics.
item.dc:creator: Juliet Macur
item.media:description: Thorns fans during a game last month at Providence Park in Portland, Ore.

item.title: Candidate Websites Are Filled With A.I.-Written Text, Analysis Shows
item.description: The use of A.I. chatbots to write candidate biographies and policy positions is another way the technology is entangled with elections.
item.dc:creator: Stuart A. Thompson and James O’Toole

item.title: Nvidia Chief, Jensen Huang, Is Seen as Target of Chinese Spy Plot
item.description: A Chinese businesswoman who had a close relationship with Jensen Huang was found to be passing intelligence to Beijing. President Trump was briefed and took no action.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Swan, Maggie Haberman, Ana Swanson, Paul Mozur, Tripp Mickle and Julian E. Barnes
item.category: Far East, South and Southeast Asia and Pacific Areas
item.media:credit: Manuel Orbegozo for The New York Times
item.media:description: Jensen Huang, the chief executive of Nvidia, is influential at the White House on technology policy and has developed a close relationship with President Trump.

item.title: Five Takeaways From the New Hampshire Senate Debate
item.description: Representative Chris Pappas and former Senator John E. Sununu both stressed their willingness to buck their parties on occasion. Neither had kind words for President Trump.
item.dc:creator: Jess Bidgood
item.media:description: Chris Pappas (left) and John E. Sununu, two veterans of Washington, each accused the other of representing the status quo.

item.title: Trump Administration Moves to Close East Potomac Park to Begin Golf Project
item.description: The government said in a court filing that it would meet the Nov. 15 deadline set by President Trump to close East Potomac Park to build a championship golf course there.
item.dc:creator: Zach Montague
item.media:credit: Andrew Leyden for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Trump administration will close most of East Potomac Park in November as part of President Trump’s plan to redevelop the municipal golf course.

item.title: In Michigan, El-Sayed Faces Heat From Former Primary Rival as Election Nears
item.description: Representative Haley Stevens has been less than enthusiastic about Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, injecting late intraparty tensions into a race that could decide Senate control.
item.dc:creator: Reid J. Epstein and Tim Balk
item.media:credit: Nic Antaya for The New York Times

item.title: Vance Proposes Restarting Peace Talks in Outreach to Iranian Official
item.description: In his letter, the vice president suggested an immediate resumption of comprehensive talks, including about Iran’s nuclear program.
item.dc:creator: Farnaz Fassihi and Tyler Pager
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
Arms Control and Limitation and Disarmament
item.media:credit: Tierney L. Cross for The New York Times
item.media:description: Vice President JD Vance is said to have made the outreach in a letter sent last week via Qatari meditators and delivered Sunday to an Iranian official, Gen. Mohsen Rezaei.

item.title: Judge Rejects Trump Officials’ Bid to Set Aside California Ballots
item.description: The judge ruled that no immediate action was necessary, dealing another setback to the administration as it moves to target voting by noncitizens.
item.dc:creator: Shawn Hubler
item.media:description: Election workers process mail-in ballots in San Diego.

item.title: Alaska Governor Orders Criminal Investigation Into Peltola Campaign
item.description: President Trump had lashed out at Mary Peltola after The New York Times reported that her campaign and national Democrats helped recruit spoiler candidates to the race. He offered no explanation of what crime may have been committed.
item.dc:creator: Kellen Browning and Anna Griffin
item.media:description: President Trump campaigned this month for Senator Dan S. Sullivan of Alaska, a Republican running for re-election this year against Mary Peltola, a Democrat and former congresswoman.

item.title: Cabinet Officials on the Campaign Trail? Ethics Experts Say Some Are Breaking the Law.
item.description: As Trump officials stump for Republican candidates facing difficult races, ethics experts say they are being lax about complying with the Hatch Act, a federal anti-corruption law.
item.dc:creator: Karoun Demirjian
item.media:description: President Trump with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick at a campaign rally in North Carolina this month.

item.title: Trump Officials Discussing Sanctions Relief for Russian Fund, Russia Acknowledges
item.description: A Russian official said potential relief for a state investment fund was part of talks. Russia has sought to wring economic benefits from the negotiations on ending the war with Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: Anton Troianovski
item.media:description: Mr. Putin’s foreign policy adviser, Yuri Ushakov, said that “such a conversation” had been “going on for some time, though I do not know what the outcome will be.”

item.title: As Trump Faces Down the Midterms, a Grim Mood Takes Over the White House
item.description: The White House has been rocked by turnover and anxiety over the midterms. The president, who is tightening his inner circle, has lashed out at critics, held meandering rallies and feasted on a diet of news clips and “A.I. slop,” as one aide put it.
item.dc:creator: Katie Rogers
item.media:description: President Trump after a campaign rally in Mississippi on Monday.

item.title: Atlanta’s Mayor Walked Away After Covid Chaos. Will Voters Make Her Georgia’s Governor?
item.description: Keisha Lance Bottoms, in her bid for Georgia governor, has faced pointed criticism of her leadership in Atlanta and disappointment in her decision to leave after one term.
item.dc:creator: Rick Rojas and Sean Keenan
item.media:description: Keisha Lance Bottoms’s campaign has been a test for what happens when a leader attempts a comeback.

item.title: Can John Sununu, a Senator Before Trump, Reclaim His New Hampshire Seat?
item.description: Plus, ballot-stacking in Alaska and a polling surprise in South Carolina.
item.dc:creator: Jess Bidgood
item.media:description: John E. Sununu in August.

item.title: Officials Back Trump’s Claim That Triumphal Arch Is Needed for National Security
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Markwayne Mullin, the homeland security secretary, submitted sworn statements to a federal court regarding the construction project.
item.dc:creator: Luke Broadwater
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:description: President Trump’s triumphal arch is slated to receive final approval next week from the National Capital Planning Commission, which is led by his allies.

item.title: Justice Dept. Turns Civil Rights Group’s Informant Against It
item.description: Lawyers for the Southern Poverty Law Center say that federal prosecutors capitalized on the informant’s money problems and exposure to indictment to persuade him to assist the government.
item.dc:creator: Alan Feuer
item.media:description: The Southern Poverty Law Center’s lawyers said that this informant went far beyond serving as a normal government witness and came to resemble a member of the government’s investigative team.

item.title: Linda McMahon Spends $43,000 on Furniture as She Looks to Close Education Department
item.description: The education secretary says her old furniture “cannot be configurationally or aesthetically integrated” into new office space.
item.dc:creator: Michael C. Bender
item.media:description: Education Secretary Linda McMahon in her old office in Washington last year.

item.title: What Does the Cheesecake Factory’s Designer Think of Obama and Trump’s Jabs at His Décor?
item.description: Long before its baroque décor and class identity became midterm talking points, this durable restaurant chain survived some withering critiques.
item.dc:creator: Kim Severson
item.media:credit: Timothy Hiatt/Getty Images for The Cheesecake Factory
item.media:description: The Cheesecake Factory has defined the term “upscale casual dining,” and closely read the psyche and the appetite of the American diner.

item.title: Gina Hinojosa’s Texas Governor Campaign Tests Limits of New Rules for Digital Political Ads
item.description: Some of the social media posts paid for by Gina Hinojosa’s campaign for Texas governor don’t include a disclosure, despite a state regulation that likely requires it.
item.dc:creator: Ken Bensinger
item.media:credit: Christopher Lee for The New York Times
item.media:description: Gina Hinojosa, the Democratic nominee for governor of Texas.

item.title: Inside Democrats’ Secret Effort to Stack Alaska’s Midterm Ballot With Another Dan Sullivan
item.description: Operatives aligned with Mary Peltola, the Democratic nominee for Senate, spent months recruiting candidates to peel votes from Senator Dan Sullivan, the Republican.
item.dc:creator: Kellen Browning
item.media:description: A sample ballot showing candidates for next week’s U.S. Senate race in Alaska lists two Dan Sullivans (highlight added here to both), along with Mary Peltola, the Democrat, and a fourth candidate named Gerald Heikes.

item.title: Democrats Eyeing 2028 Presidential Campaigns Begin Courting Donors and Operatives
item.description: As soon as the midterms are over, presidential contenders are going to need to raise millions, quickly.
item.dc:creator: Theodore Schleifer
item.media:description: From left, Govs. Gavin Newsom of California, Andy Beshear of Kentucky, Josh Shapiro of Pennsylvania and Wes Moore of Maryland are all potential 2028 presidential candidates.
